clue.text: Crackers — batch mishandled by one engaged in dubious exchanges

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a person trading favours, matching the noun answer

indicators.note: a batch handled badly gets jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A batch of Christmas crackers is botched by a shady dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like the anagram signal (mad) but is fodder; 'mishandled' shuffles CRACKERS with BATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trades mutual favours, you-scratch-mine style, is engaged in dubious exchanges.

clue.text: I err — a tab, but it's wrong drug

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Admitting a mistake with a pill, but it's the wrong medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbiturate is a sedative drug.

clue.text: River bank robber

definitions.meaning: a Scottish river flowing through Glasgow
the Depression-era outlaw partner of Bonnie Parker

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a Scottish waterway and the first name of the outlaw Barrow.

clue.text: One insect nailed by certain characteristic

indicators.note: pinned inside, as the insect is held within the certain word

parts.note: sure means certain
I is one
a gnat is a small insect

explanation.surface: A single bug is definitely pinned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature style or dish is the one that marks someone out, their distinctive trait.

clue.text: Take over from old official, about 51

indicators.note: the official goes around the number

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval local magistrate
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Replacing a former officer who is about fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' is part of the definition of REEVE, not O.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a sentry or worker is to take over their duty from them.

clue.text: Rise of young man with sex appeal that's ebbing and flowing

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise reads from the bottom up, so the pieces go backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A handsome lad's star goes up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes the sea's rise and fall, its ebb and flow.

clue.text: Draw attention to the moon, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the moon is one example of a light high in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: To spotlight something is to emphasise it; read as two words, a lamp up above, such as the moon.

clue.text: 21 in port

definitions.meaning: a cereal plant of the family named by the answer to 21 down
a Cinque Port town in East Sussex

explanation.definitionFit: It is a cereal crop of the weed family named at 21, and also an old harbour town in Sussex.

clue.text: Proclaim loudly where musical vicar lived

definitions.meaning: to bellow or blare like a donkey
the turncoat Vicar of the old song lived in this village

explanation.surface: A clergyman known for song announces his parish at the top of his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is the subject of an 18th-century English song about a priest who changed his creed with every monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's harsh cry gives a verb for shouting something out noisily; the song names the parish of Bray.

clue.text: Determined, dogged girl —- one after your money

indicators.note: read as 'settled by rearrangement', telling us the following letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A resolute, persistent young woman turns out to be chasing your cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Determined, dogged' reads as two adjectives describing the girl; 'Determined' is in fact the anagram signal acting on DOGGED GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who courts someone for their wealth is the classic mercenary suitor chasing money.

clue.text: £1? Carpet is free!

parts.note: L is the pound sign's letter (libra) and I is one
to carpet someone is to scold them, to berate

explanation.surface: A rug offered for a pound is as good as given away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb meaning to reprimand, not the floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone free is to release them, a straightforward synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Sucker drops one penny in lounge

indicators.note: the sucker lets go of some letters, so they are removed from it

parts.note: a lollipop is a sweet on a stick that you suck
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A con man's victim loses a coin while relaxing in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room but is the verb: to lounge or loll about.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move or sprawl in a lazy, relaxed way, as one does when lounging.

clue.text: Rapturous reception overwhelms Serb after translating comment

indicators.note: the applause engulfs the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: an ovation is enthusiastic applause

indicators.note: the letters are changed into another form, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild applause drowns out a Serbian's remark once it is interpreted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapturous reception' suggests a welcome party, but it is the standing applause that 'overwhelms' (contains) the 'translating' anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation is a remark or comment.

clue.text: Super daughter struggling on sort of bike — perhaps horses wanted

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a quad bike is a four-wheeled motorbike

indicators.note: letters that are struggling are in disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A superb daughter battles on a quad bike when what she really wants is horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' is a link word tacked on for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are an example of four-footed animals, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Courageous action going wrong during strange rising

indicators.note: the wrongdoing sits inside the strange word
in a down clue, rising reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: odd means strange
erring means going wrong

explanation.surface: A brave act misfires amid a bizarre revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym; 'rising' reverses only 'strange', and 'during' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring, heroic action.

clue.text: In the middle of the street, tiny Frenchman turned up for a bribe

indicators.note: the tiny word sits within the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
wee means tiny

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up reads backwards

parts.note: René is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A small French man appears in the street to offer a backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the middle of' is a container signal here, not a pick of central letters; 'turned up' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement given to win someone over, a bribe.

clue.text: Score extra

definitions.meaning: to score is to cut a line or deep wound into something
in slang, especially military, the word means surplus or spare

explanation.definitionFit: A deep cut is a score mark; the slang sense of spare or surplus gives the second meaning.

clue.text: Strong wind, but not cloudy

parts.note: F is forte, loud or strong in music
air is a breath or current of wind

explanation.surface: A gale is blowing, though the sky is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong wind' reads as a gale but splits: F (forte) plus AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather means clear skies, the opposite of cloudy.

clue.text: Simple alert —- enemy is on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifting about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain warning: hostile forces are advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or easy, a direct synonym for simple.

clue.text: Part I've got is mainly a show of conceit

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: My role is mostly vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive self-regard displayed in behaviour, a display of vanity.

clue.text: Margaret carrying family to capital in days of yore

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a bearer carries a load

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: Margaret takes her relatives to the old capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is now Beijing, so the older romanisation belongs to days of yore.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the older Western name for China's capital, now romanised as Beijing.

clue.text: Weed in lawn

explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is slang weed, and a lawn is turf, both the same plant word.

clue.text: Epidemic of disease really halved in the old country

indicators.note: the disease and the half-word go inside the country

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
TB is tuberculosis

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A disease spreads across a nation that has been cut in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old country' looks like one phrase but splits: 'old' is a letter of its own and 'the' is padding; 'halved' keeps the front half.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is a sudden spread of disease, so it names an epidemic.

clue.text: State takes on surgeon to provide a fix

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A state employs a surgeon to make a repair.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten something firmly with a metal pin.

clue.text: Race, primarily for men, coming to a standstill

indicators.note: the stag piece comes first, ahead of the race piece

parts.note: a stag event is for men only
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A male-only race grinds to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' looks like a first-letter signal but just says the men piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is the state of being stalled, a noun for things grinding to a halt.

clue.text: From consultant, finally a good stock quotation

indicators.note: take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A consultant ends on a good familiar saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock quotation' suggests share prices but means a hackneyed saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a well-worn phrase or quotation.

clue.text: Style-bootless by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word is judged by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: bootless is an old word for useless or in vain

explanation.surface: Fashion without boots, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bootless' has nothing to do with footwear; it means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a manner or mood, as in writing in a comic strain.

clue.text: Merchandise a girl handed in to man, a helpful fellow

parts.note: goods are merchandise

indicators.note: the girl is put inside the man

parts.note: taken as written
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl delivers merchandise to a man, a kindly chap.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' belongs to the definition; the first stands alone, and 'handed in to' places the girl inside the man.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable, a person who helps a stranger in need is a byword for a kind helper.
